column4: S8.3: the sound argument of BinkPlayer::play is resourceQuery's result (playAudioFile 0x0043cd45, on g_musicDevice 0x0083ad80: slot +0x74 of the object at +0x14, 0 when that pointer is NULL). The module passes 0, the value of every recorded run (device-less sound library, S8.2 U-1713); a non-zero value only makes the original call _BinkSetSoundSystem (0x004870b2) before the open, which writes no GameState word, so the port's state is the same for any value. What a decoder host must do with the sound system when a device exists is not measured.
column5: Record a run with an audio device (C3FT_AUDIO=live) and read resourceQuery's return and the _BinkSetSoundSystem call; give MovieHost::open the value if a decoder needs it.

column4: S8.3: input during a playing movie is modelled, not measured. The port gives each not-due pass of BinkPlayer::play two Drain pumps (pumpInput483c90 with g_inputPhase 2, pumpInput483cf0 with 8) and the emulator oracle delivers a scripted key through frameTick483cd0, which only pumpInput483cf0 reaches (redrawAll 0x00483c70 is a stub there, as in every cmdemu oracle). In the original both pumps reach jgld display slots that dispatch window messages (+0x134 from redrawAll, +0x13c from frameTick483cd0), so which of the two pumps takes a message that arrives during a movie depends on jgld, and no recording delivers one (S8.2 U-1710). Only a decoder host with live input meets this.
column5: With U-1710's real WM_KEYDOWN during the intro, log which of the two pumps' dispatch calls the root handler and the pass count at BinkClose.

The gfx backend has no body for Window::paint, so a gfx run's back buffer after a skipped movie is whatever it held; the pinned skip-intro checkpoints show the original's (no movie frame was ever captured, S8.2 U-1711).
